chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): What do you say regarding a man who prepares for Ihram and is free from everything except that he has not said the Talbiyah? Is it permissible for him to break that state and have intercourse with women? He said: Yes.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: The ritual declaration 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' marking entry into Ihram
key_terms.يَنْقُض: To break or nullify (the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim break Ihram and have sex before reciting Talbiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the binding state of Ihram is contingent upon the recitation of the Talbiyah, meaning preparatory acts like washing and donning garments do not yet incur the prohibitions of Ihram. Consequently, a pilgrim may validly engage in marital relations before this declaration, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on the verbal intent (Niyyah) as the precise moment of legal commitment. This ruling underscores the distinction between physical preparation and the formalization of the pilgrimage ritual.
